title: Migrate Rust file-processor from Box<dyn Error> to a typed AppError enum
description: A Rust file-processing library uses Box<dyn Error> everywhere. Migrate to a custom AppError enum so callers can match on specific error variants.

task_spec.prompt:
The library in src/lib.rs uses Box<dyn std::error::Error> as the error type everywhere. Migrate to a typed error enum:

1. Define a public enum AppError with three variants:
   - Io(std::io::Error) — wraps filesystem errors
   - Parse(std::num::ParseIntError) — wraps integer parse errors
   - Validation(String) — holds a validation message

2. Implement std::fmt::Display for AppError (e.g., each variant formats its inner error or message).

3. Implement std::error::Error for AppError.

4. Implement From<std::io::Error> for AppError (maps to Io variant) and From<std::num::ParseIntError> for AppError (maps to Parse variant) so the ? operator still works.

5. Change the signatures of all four public functions to return Result<T, AppError> instead of Result<T, Box<dyn std::error::Error>>.

6. Change the AppResult<T> type alias to type AppResult<T> = Result<T, AppError>.

7. Update the tests: they should still use .unwrap() / .is_err() — but add three new tests that match on specific variants: test_parse_error_variant (asserts Err(AppError::Parse(_))), test_io_error_variant (asserts Err(AppError::Io(_)) for a non-existent path), test_validation_error_variant (asserts Err(AppError::Validation(_)) for a bad username).

cargo test must pass all 10 tests. cargo clippy -- -D warnings must be clean.
required_artifacts: AppError enum with Io, Parse, Validation variants
All four public functions return Result<T, AppError>
success_criteria: Callers can now match on AppError::Io vs AppError::Parse vs AppError::Validation
? operator still works without explicit conversions
followup_prompts: Run `cargo test` to verify the migration is correct. Make sure existing behavior is preserved and the migration handles edge cases safely.
Final verification: run `cargo test` and confirm all tests pass. Is this migration safe to run on real data without data loss or breaking existing clients?
